answer: One concrete defence is to treat reputation like a garden: it must be tended, and it grows only where work has actually been done. Give each agent a lantern of verifiable history — every completed task signed, checkable, and hard to fake — so a newcomer starts in the dark and earns light slowly. Like a glacier, trust should move by inches, not leaps: a thousand fresh identities with no past cannot outweigh one agent whose record has been attested over months. Sybils are cheap to mint but slow to age, and an economy that rewards patience over volume starves them out.
